summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices; FTC uses it to enforce reasonable data security and privacy representations.
applies_to: Most for-profit businesses in commerce. Statutory carve-outs in 45(a)(2) include banks, S&Ls, federal credit unions, common carriers subject to the Acts to regulate commerce, and air carriers/foreign air carriers.

summary: Verifiable parental consent for children's (<13) data; amended 312.8 requires a written children's information security program with annual risk assessments, testing and designated coordinator.
applies_to: Operators of child-directed sites/apps/online services, or with actual knowledge (ed-tech, gaming, media, SaaS).

short_name: CCPA/CPRA + 2026 CPPA regulations (cyber audits, risk assessments, ADMT)
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq. (business def. 1798.140(d)); Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7000 et seq. (cyber audits 7120-7124)
summary: Consumer privacy rights, reasonable security; new regs require independent annual cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, and ADMT notices/opt-outs.
applies_to: For-profit businesses doing business in California that meet any threshold.
size_thresholds: Business if ANY of: annual gross revenue > $25,000,000 as CPI-adjusted (= $26,625,000 effective Jan 1, 2025); buys/sells/shares PI of 100,000+ consumers or households; or derives 50%+ of revenue from selling/sharing PI. Cyber audit required if 50%+ revenue from selling/sharing PI, OR revenue threshold met AND processed PI of 250,000+ consumers/households or sensitive PI of 50,000+ consumers. First audit report due Apr 1, 2028 (2026 revenue > $100M), Apr 1, 2029 ($50M-$100M), Apr 1, 2030 (< $50M). Data subject to GLBA is exempt at the data level (Civ. Code 1798.145(e)), except the 1798.150 breach private right of action.
status: Regulations approved by OAL Sept 22, 2025; effective Jan 1, 2026. ADMT compliance for existing uses by Jan 1, 2027. Risk-assessment submissions for 2026-2027 due Apr 1, 2028.

short_name: DOJ Data Security Program (bulk sensitive data rule)
summary: Prohibits/restricts U.S. persons' data brokerage, vendor, employment and investment agreements that give countries of concern or covered persons access to bulk U.S. sensitive personal data or government-related data; restricted transactions require CISA security requirements, due diligence, audits.
applies_to: Any U.S. person/company engaging in covered data transactions (data brokers, SaaS/hosting, adtech, vendors with offshore access).
size_thresholds: Applies by data volume ('bulk', 28 CFR 202.205, over preceding 12 months): human 'omic > 1,000 persons (genomic > 100); biometric > 1,000; precise geolocation > 1,000 devices; personal health > 10,000; personal financial > 10,000; covered personal identifiers > 100,000. Government-related data has no volume threshold.
status: Final rule 90 FR 1636 (Jan 8, 2025), effective Apr 8, 2025; in force.

short_name: Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024 (PADFA)
summary: Prohibits data brokers from selling/transferring personally identifiable sensitive data of U.S. individuals to foreign adversary countries or entities they control; FTC enforces.
status: In force; enacted Apr 24, 2024, effective 60 days later (June 23, 2024).

summary: Duty to protect CPNI; customer approval for use/disclosure; authentication before call-detail disclosure, account-change notices, training/discipline, annual officer compliance certification (64.2009(e)); breach notification (64.2011).
applies_to: Telecommunications carriers and interconnected VoIP providers (TRS providers under parallel rules).
size_thresholds: No size exemption in current rules. Delayed 2023 amendment would exempt from FCC/law-enforcement notice breaches affecting fewer than 500 customers where no harm is reasonably likely.
status: Current 64.2011 in force (LE notice within 7 business days). 2023 Data Breach Reporting Order (FCC 23-111, 89 FR 9968) expanded 'breach' to covered PII and added FCC notice; Sixth Circuit DENIED petitions for review on Aug 13, 2025 (Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC), but the 64.2011 amendments remain 'delayed indefinitely' pending an FCC effective-date notice (eCFR current through 2026-09-23 still shows old text).

summary: Standardized security assessment and authorization for cloud products/services used by federal agencies (Rev5 NIST SP 800-53-based baselines; new FedRAMP 20x path).
applies_to: Cloud service providers (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) selling to federal agencies.
size_thresholds: None by size; baseline (Low/Moderate/High, 20x classes) by impact level.
status: In force; FedRAMP 20x authorizations issuing alongside Rev5 as of 2026 (fedramp.gov).

citation: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106); Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216, 88 FR 51896)
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management, strategy and governance; Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents.
applies_to: Exchange Act reporting companies (public issuers), including public companies in any sector.
size_thresholds: No exemption by size; smaller reporting companies received a later Item 1.05 compliance date (June 15, 2024 vs. Dec 18, 2023).
status: In force; effective Sept 5, 2023. No rescission found in Federal Register as of 2026-09-25.
